title: The remote passed pawn as a decoy

D0.outcome: Explains a remote passed pawn used as a decoy: prepare the king's journey before the diverting sacrifice or exchange.

D1.outcome: In a pawn ending with a remote passer, plans the king route that wins the pawns on the other wing.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled endings, decides when to push the remote passer and when to hold it back, and uses zugzwang to entice enemy pawns forward.

D3.outcome: Predicts the effect of spending the passer too early and verifies with counting and the tablebase.

misconceptions: Push a passed pawn simply because it is passed.
conditions: The king's journey is prepared before the diverting sacrifice; the enemy pawns are enticed forward by zugzwang.
contrasts: Spending the remote passer too early.
Advancing the pawn when it neither nears promotion nor wins ground.
A position with no remote passer.
note: The map names END.REMOTE without a definition; here read as the remote passed pawn (Nimzowitsch's term). Flagged in the report as an ambiguity.
